title: Which of Your Lord's Favors Would You Deny?

paragraphs.text: The Most Merciful created man and taught him how to speak clearly and express himself. The sun and the moon move according to an exact calculation, never going off their course. The stars and the trees bow down in prostration to Him. He raised the sky high and set up the balance, so that people would not go beyond limits in it. Therefore, they must weigh with justice and must never cheat by giving less than the right measure. In this way, the order of the universe is connected with the honesty that people must show in their daily dealings.

Allah spread out the earth for all His creatures. On it there are fruits, and palm trees whose dates grow inside covers. There is also grain with its husks and plants with sweet smells. After describing these blessings, the surah asks for the first time a question that it will repeat many times: "So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?" It invites the reader to stop and count the many good things he enjoys every day.

Allah created man from dry clay like that used for pottery, and He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. Again the question is asked: which of the Lord's favors would they deny? He is the Lord of the two sunrises and the Lord of the two sunsets, so both the beginning and the end of each day are in His hands. Once more, the same question follows, inviting each listener to look honestly at all he has been given.

Allah also released the two seas, so that they meet side by side. This passage continues in the following verses, but already the reader sees how every part of nature, from the sky to the earth and the seas, is presented as a favor that no one can truly deny.
